predecessors.name: Venad
predecessors.text: Venad: Kalkulam and Padmanabhapuram to Thiruvananthapuram

successors.name: Travancore-Cochin
successors.text: Travancore with Ambalapuzha, Kottayam, Changanassery, Karappuram and Alangad: the kingdom of 1753-1949

ledger.x: 1729: Marthanda Varma becomes king of Venad and builds Travancore.
1731: Marthanda Varma's first target, the port of Kollam (Quilon).
1743-1752: Thekkumkur, Vadakkumkur and Purakkad are annexed.
By 1753: Ambalapuzha, Kottayam and Changanassery are annexed.
1795: Dharma Raja moves the capital from Padmanabhapuram to Thiruvananthapuram.

wars.name: Travancore-Dutch War
wars.outcome: Travancore beat the Dutch at Colachel on 10 August 1741; the Treaty of Mavelikkara of 15 August 1753 closed the war.

wars.name: Annexation of the Kerala principalities
wars.outcome: Marthanda Varma annexed Kollam, Kottarakkara, Kayamkulam, Thekkumkur, Vadakkumkur, Purakkad, Ambalapuzha, Kottayam and Changanassery between 1731 and 1753; Kochi ceded Karappuram and Alangad; Zamorin of Kozhikode beaten at Purakkad in 1755.

wars.name: Mysore invasion of Travancore
wars.outcome: Tipu Sultan attacked Travancore in 1789 and the Nedunkotta lines on 28 December 1789; the page names no Travancore territory lost.

certainty.note: Principalities annexed one by one; the pages name chiefdoms and towns, not boundaries, so the shapes are latitude bands of the Kerala coast.
The page gives no boundary line; the northern limit near Alangad is approximate (shape 19,000 km2 against 19,844 km2).
